title: Quadratic String Concatenation in Loops (Accumulator Starvation)
pattern: A string or vector is constructed incrementally in a loop by repeatedly using the `+` operator, creating a new allocated string/vector and copying the accumulated data on each iteration.
why_bad: While locally appearing "simple" and clear, it has quadratic $O(N^2)$ complexity. Each string addition allocates fresh heap memory, copies the old data into the new buffer, and deallocates the old buffer. For thousands of elements, this causes severe garbage collection and heap fragmentation pressure.
detection: Loops that repeatedly append data using concatenation (`+` operator on strings) instead of utilizing a single pre-allocated mutable builder or accumulator buffer.
counterexample: Concatenating 2 or 3 static strings is perfectly fine and often optimized by the compiler.
source: Joshua Kerievsky, *Refactoring to Patterns*, "Collecting Parameter" (p. 379) / Martin Fowler, *Refactoring*, "Removing Temps" (p. 586).
